run.summary: I ran 5 lanes in 2 round(s) and asked for 2 independent re-check(s), always for the strongest development gain. These replicated: e001 (A quadratic trend extrapolates better than a straight line.); e004 (The readings follow a damped oscillation exp(-g t) (A cos(w t) + B sin(w t)) + C with an u). These improved on the development data but were not re-checked or did not replicate, so they are not findings: e005. The current best is e004, which replicated. The re-check says only pass or fail, so I report no size for the gain. Caveat: one task, a small pool of measurements, and the development numbers are optimistic because they were used to choose lanes.

experiments.hypothesis: A quadratic trend extrapolates better than a straight line.
A flexible degree-9 polynomial can follow the oscillation and so extrapolates better.
A tiny ridge penalty on the straight line makes its extrapolation more conservative.
The readings follow a damped oscillation exp(-g t) (A cos(w t) + B sin(w t)) + C with an unknown decay g and frequency w.
Choosing the polynomial degree and ridge strength by backtesting on the latest part of the training window beats a fixed degree.
